title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A Georgia couple was defrauded of nearly $800,000 through a cryptocurrency scheme in which scammers used a fake AI-generated website to display false investment balances. The scammers had contacted the victim via WhatsApp and directed him to a legitimate mobile trading app, but then presented fabricated account information designed to convince him his investments were growing. The false information was shown directly on the victim's screen, making it appear authentic.

The failure occurred in the gap between a legitimate financial application and the information presented to the user. A human verification step, such as independent confirmation of account balances through official channels before allowing large withdrawals, could have exposed the discrepancy. The scam was sophisticated enough to overcome the victim's initial caution by allowing small successful transactions before requesting larger investments.

It is not established whether the legitimate trading app had any role in enabling the scheme, whether the fake website was a copy of an existing site, or what specific AI generation techniques were used to create the fraudulent balance displays.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest using a mobile trading app, and initially allowed him to make small trades and withdraw money to build trust. Over time, Dunaway increased his investments significantly. When he tried to withdraw a larger amount last week, he discovered the funds were inaccessible and contacted police.

Investigators determined that while the trading app was legitimate, scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that showed false investment balances on Dunaway's screen. The couple, who lost their entire life savings, is now speaking publicly to warn others about the sophisticated tactics used by scammers. Though working with Gwinnett County police, authorities say victims in these cases rarely recover their money. The Dunaways' children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help their parents with daily expenses.
